title: A Noetherian finite stratification for separated quasi-finite morphisms
statement: Let $v:V\to X$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Suppose $X$ is Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Then there is a finite scheme stratification $S$ of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification] such that the pullback $V\times_X S_a\to S_a$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] for every stratum. Here locally quasi-finite may be read as Mathlib's ring-theoretic predicate: the separate local finite-type hypothesis makes it the usual Stacks notion.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof of part (1)

proof.text: Use Noetherian induction on closed subsets Z of X. If Z is empty take the empty family. Otherwise choose an irreducible component of Z and a nonempty open of Z meeting only that component. Give its closure the reduced closed subscheme structure and base change v to it. The base-changed map remains locally quasi-finite, separated and quasi-compact, so it is quasi-finite. The generic finite-neighborhood theorem gives a neighborhood of the generic point over which it is finite.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof of part (1)

proof.text: Intersect this neighborhood with the chosen component-open. Its image is a nonempty locally closed piece of Z with closed complement. The induced immersion has finite pullback of v by restriction stability and pullback pasting. Apply the induction hypothesis to the strictly smaller closed complement and take the disjoint union of the two finite families. The resulting locally closed pieces cover X uniquely. Reindex by Fin n; in a Noetherian scheme their locally closed images are constructible, giving a Scheme.Stratification X. This is the already proved source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_stratification_isFinite, reused without a new proof.
